limitations: The finite query ownership case uses two service identities and two query slots for one agent. TaskScheduler retains the model for dirty agents, busy services, generations and dispatch.
Runtime closure follows the existing host contract to stop its services first. The host owns the shared adapter lifetime across all runtimes and must await scheduler stop before closing that adapter.
Per-service worker and preflight drainage are covered separately by TaskRetirement. Query ownership does not cancel a hung adapter call.

Real PGlite conformance delays a real adapter query and injects a stale query failure after reading actual storage. Multiple agents in one batch and concurrent independent schedulers remain outside this model.
